evidence: src/domain/TaskStatus.ts holds the only definition of TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus. src/domain/Task.ts (Task.create uses isTaskStatus) and src/domain/TaskRepository.ts (TaskFilter.status: TaskStatus) reuse them.
src/domain/errors.ts defines DomainError and its subclasses ValidationError, NotFoundError and TaskAlreadyDoneError. Project.ts, User.ts and Task.ts throw only these classes.
src/domain/Project.ts, User.ts and Task.ts all use a private constructor and a static create() factory that checks the entity's invariants.
src/domain/ProjectRepository.ts, TaskRepository.ts and UserRepository.ts are all persistence ports with the same shape: save and findById, plus findByProject on TaskRepository.
The task-completion rule is only in Task.markDone in src/domain/Task.ts, which throws TaskAlreadyDoneError from src/domain/errors.ts.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain is one cohesive domain model for project and task management. It has three entities (Project, Task, User), one repository port for each entity, a TaskStatus value type, and a single error hierarchy. Every invariant lives in one place. The allowed status values are defined only in TaskStatus.ts (TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus, isTaskStatus). Task.ts and TaskRepository.ts reuse them instead of redefining them. All domain failures go through the DomainError subclasses in errors.ts, and no file throws a raw Error. Each entity checks its own rules in a private-constructor plus static create() factory, so the abstraction is used the same way throughout. Project.create and User.create look alike: each trims a name and throws ValidationError. These are separate invariants for separate entities, not one shared rule copied in two places, so they are not a violation. No file bypasses the module's abstractions.
